title: Philippines' textile & apparel imports fall 4.65% in Jan-Sept 2026
summary:
Philippines’ combined textile and apparel imports fell 4.65 per cent year on year to $1.662 billion in January–September 2026, while exports slipped 0.38 per cent to $765.82 million, PSA data showed.
Textile yarn, fabric and made-up imports dropped 8.50 per cent, outweighing higher apparel imports.
September trade improved, with imports up 1.90 per cent and exports up 1.42 per cent year on year.

title: Philippines' manufacturing PMI falls to 49.1 in October
summary:
Philippines manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.1 in October from 49.6 in September, signalling a second straight monthly deterioration in factory conditions, S&P Global said.
Output and new orders stayed in contraction, while purchasing activity fell at the fastest pace in 11 months.
Employment declined again, but business confidence rebounded to a near two-year high.

title: Vietnam’s trade surplus climbs sharply to $7.31 bn in October
summary:
Vietnam recorded a $7.31 billion trade surplus in October after a $1.3 billion surplus in September, its second consecutive monthly surplus in 2026, NSO data showed.
October trade reached $122.03 billion, up 3.7 per cent month on month and 47.4 per cent year on year.
January-October turnover hit a record $1.01 trillion; exports were $499.24 billion and imports $511.31 billion.

title: Bank of England raises interest rate to 4% as inflation risks mount
summary:
The Bank of England raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 4 per cent, warning that UK inflation could reach around 5 per cent by mid-2027 as the Middle East conflict pushes up energy prices. 
The MPC voted 8-1 for the increase, citing stronger-than-expected economic activity and growing risks of persistent inflationary pressures.

title: Brazil cotton prices fall in October as weak demand weighs on market
summary:
Brazil’s cotton prices fell 4.47 per cent month on month in October 2026 amid weak demand and cautious trading, although a weaker real supported a late-month recovery. 
Global cotton production is forecast to decline 4 per cent in 2026-27 to 25.75 million tonnes, while consumption is expected to rise 0.8 per cent to 26.1 million tonnes, creating a projected supply deficit of 353,000 tonnes, ICAC said.

title: Australian wool market shows signs of stabilisation in November
summary:
Australia's wool market eased for a fourth week, with the EMI down 25 cents to 1,698 Auc/kg and 21 cents lower in US-dollar terms.
Australian Wool Innovation said 25,022 bales were offered, 21,618 sold and the pass-in rate halved to 13.6 per cent.
Superfine clearances improved, but crossbred indicators stayed under pressure ahead of a 30,919-bale Week 20 forecast.

title: US cotton export sales rise 28%, but shipments hit to year low
summary:
US Upland cotton net sales rose 28 per cent to 277,500 RB in the week ended October 29, 53 per cent above the four-week average, with Vietnam the top buyer at 200,500 RB.
Upland shipments fell 14 per cent to a marketing-year low of 137,800 RB.
Pima sales rebounded to 6,400 RB, led by India, while shipments more than doubled from 3,300 RB to 7,100 RB.

title: Hyosung TNC profit jumps 97%, but can bio-spandex transform its future
summary:
Hyosung TNC’s preliminary Q3 revenue reached KRW 2,133.1 billion, up 6.1 per cent year on year but down 11.7 per cent from Q2.
Operating profit was KRW 110.2 billion, up 96.7 per cent year on year but 41.6 per cent lower sequentially; nine-month profit rose 86.3 per cent.
Spandex volumes fell after Q2 restocking, prices stayed flat and brands can assess certified lower-carbon spandex.

title: Global cotton faces a 353,000-tonne deficit: Why are prices falling?
summary:
Projected 2027 global cotton deficits mask swelling Chinese stocks, weak yarn movement and price pressure, leaving mills exposed to sourcing risks.
ICAC sees a 353,000-tonne 2026-27 deficit, while USDA estimates 1.12 million tonnes, but global ending stocks remain near 15.39 million tonnes.
TexPro shows China’s yarn imports rising as Brazil exports grow and India and Pakistan import more cotton.

title: Bangladesh's BRAC Bank cuts export document processing to one day
summary:
BRAC Bank completed Bangladesh’s first fully digital, end-to-end export documentary collection for a garment shipment to the UK, cutting document processing time from 40 days to one using blockchain technology and electronic trade documents. 
The transaction involved NAZ Bangladesh, Matalan and Lloyds Bank, the bank said.

title: Japan's Goldwin cuts FY27 outlook as H1 operating profit falls 31.7%
summary:
Japan's Goldwin reported a 0.9 per cent rise in H1 FY27 sales to ¥56.09 billion (~$355.37 million), while operating profit fell 31.7 per cent to ¥4.76 billion (~$30.16 million).
Gross margin improved to 52.8 per cent.

title: US' Nike advances sportswear with four FIT technologies
summary:
Nike explains its FIT performance-apparel system, first introduced in 1991 and developed through athlete testing, material innovation and sport science research.
The four technologies are Dri-FIT for dryness, Aero-FIT for cooling, Therma-FIT for warmth and Storm-FIT for protection from the elements across sports and changing running conditions.

title: Bangladesh RMG sector: Can it stay on course amid challenges?
summary:
Bangladesh’s RMG sector faces buyer-confidence risks after wage protests halted more than 500 factories on November 1 and nearly 700 the next day.
Earlier gas and power shortages cut daily gas supply by 450–500 million cubic feet and caused 30–40 per cent production-capacity losses.
A six-member wage board aims to set revised pay by December 2026, with new wages to be paid in January 2027.

title: Sri Lanka's garment exports fall 5.3% to $3.52 bn in Jan–Sep 2026

Textile exports dropped 8.0 per cent to $201.0 million and other manufactured textile articles slid 12.3 per cent to $78.5 million.
September textile and garment exports rose 3.6 per cent year on year to $441.4 million, but nine-month textile imports fell 3.7 per cent.

title: US study finds polyester T-shirts raise microplastic exposure by 42%
summary:
University of Memphis pilot findings suggest fabric type may affect microplastic levels in the personal breathing zone, with polyester T-shirts raising exposure by up to 42 per cent over cotton.
The study involved 10 participants wearing cotton and polyester-containing T-shirts, plus 12-hour bedroom baseline air measurements.
PET was found among 99 per cent of detected airborne microplastics.

title: Bangladesh garment crisis: Can 690 factories regain buyer confidence?
summary:
Bangladesh’s garment sector faces buyer concern after wage protests led nearly 690 factories to suspend production, though many later reopened.
Workers seek a Tk 30,000 (~$241), monthly minimum, up from Tk 12,500; a revised scale is due from December but no amount is agreed.
Exports fell 1.64 per cent in fiscal 2025-26, while TexPro shows pressure in US-bound T-shirts and men’s woven clothing.
